rows.description: A friend notices someone saying nothing will ever change and giving away possessions or withdrawing. Persistent hopelessness deserves a direct caring conversation and involvement of professional help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child insists their team will surely win or that a lost pet will return tomorrow. Childlike optimism protects from fear but can shatter painfully when reality arrives.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, hope, hurt

rows.description: A teenager expects the worst on every exam so that any result feels like a win. Lowering expectations shields feelings, though it can also quietly reduce effort.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A grieving or failing student is told just think positive and feels more alone. Forced cheer dismisses real difficulty and blocks honest conversation.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A person names the real obstacles, then decides what can be done and proceeds with confidence in their ability to adapt. Optimism about effort with realism about odds is more durable than either alone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A colleague says I am just being realistic every time a new idea appears, and never tries. Cynicism can pass for wisdom, but real realism still risks something.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A toddler opens every drawer, tastes leaves and pulls things apart. Curiosity is the engine of early learning, and safety-proofing works better than constant saying no.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A child asks why the sky is blue, why grandma is old, why the moon follows the car. Answers matter less than an adult who treats the questions as worth answering.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A child who is told do not ask silly questions in class stops asking, though the curiosity persists privately or fades. Dismissive responses teach a child that wonder is unwelcome.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: playfulness, curiosity, awe

rows.description: A teenager explores sex, religion, risky videos or rebellious ideas partly from real interest. Curiosity that is met with panic goes underground, while calm answers keep the door open.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 23–26
related mind states: curiosity, interest, calm
